record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Possible extra asymptotic regimes for partial shattering
record.original_question: Fix k > 3 and let P be a family of permutations of [n]. For each t, write m_{k,t}(n) for the minimum size of a family P that t-shatters every k-subset of [n]. Outside the three regimes already known in Theorem 14.2, are there any values of t for which the extremal order of growth of m_{k,t}(n) is in a different asymptotic regime than t, Θ(log log n), or Θ(log n)?

evidence.quote: As before, the same three regimes appear, but it is unknown what happens to the size of P when t lies in the range [k + 1, 2(k − 1)!]. In particular, we have the following questions: • Are there any values of t for which the size of an extremal family is not in one of these three regimes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k \geq 4$ be a fixed integer and let $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. A family $\mathcal{P}$ of permutations of $[n]$ is said to $t$-shatter a $k$-subset $S = \{s_1 < s_2 < \dots < s_k\} \subseteq [n]$ if, among the $k!$ possible linear orders that the elements of $S$ can take, at least $t$ distinct orders are realized by restricting some permutation in $\mathcal{P}$ to $S$. Define
$$m_{k,t}(n) = \min\{|\mathcal{P}| : \mathcal{P}\text{ is a family of permutations of }[n]\text{ that }t\text{-shatters every }k\text{-subset of }[n]\}.$$
It is known that for the three "extremal" values of $t$ (namely $t = 2$, $t = k!$, and certain intermediate boundary cases), as $n \to \infty$, $m_{k,t}(n)$ falls into one of the asymptotic regimes: bounded (constant in $n$), $\Theta(\log\log n)$, or $\Theta(\log n)$.

Question: For $k > 3$, does there exist a value of $t \in \{2,3,\dots,k!\}$ such that the order of growth of $m_{k,t}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$ is not of order constant, $\Theta(\log\log n)$, or $\Theta(\log n)$, i.e., lies in a genuinely different asymptotic regime?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 work by Girão and collaborators ("Small families of partially shattering permutations", arXiv:2407.05773) answers the question affirmatively: for $k \geq 4$ there exist values of $t$ for which $m_{k,t}(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{\log n})$, giving a fourth asymptotic regime distinct from constant, $\Theta(\log\log n)$, and $\Theta(\log n)$.

status_evidence.title: Small families of partially shattering permutations
status_evidence.snippet: A fourth regime exists for k ≥ 4 with f_k(n,t) = Θ(√log n) for certain values of t.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes a fourth asymptotic regime of order √log n for the partial shattering permutation problem when k ≥ 4.

status_evidence.title: Shattering k-sets with Permutations
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier work establishing the three known regimes for partial shattering by permutations.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the baseline three regimes (constant, log log n, log n) that the question asks to go beyond.
